description: Compute n! for any n from 0 to 170. See the exact value, scientific notation, the multiplication expanded step by step and the count of trailing zeros.

faqs.a: n! (n factorial) is the product of all positive integers from 1 to n. For example, 5! = 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 120. By definition, 0! = 1.
170! is the largest factorial that fits in a standard 64-bit floating-point number (about 7.26 × 10^306). 171! overflows to infinity.
Each trailing zero comes from a factor of 10 = 2 × 5. Since factors of 2 are plentiful, the count equals the number of factors of 5 in 1…n: floor(n/5) + floor(n/25) + floor(n/125) + …

howto: Enter a whole number n between 0 and 170.
The factorial value appears instantly, exact for n ≤ 18.
Read the scientific-notation form for large values.
See the trailing-zero count and, for n ≤ 10, the full multiplication expanded.
title: Factorial Calculator
